question.problem: Let $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2\end{aligned}].$ What are the coordinates of $x$ relative to the basis $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\},$ where ${c}_{1}=2{b}_{1}-{b}_{2}$ and ${c}_{2}={b}_{2}-{b}_{1}?$
question.worked_solution:
We are given that

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}=2{b}_{1}-{b}_{2} \\ {c}_{2}=-{b}_{1}+{b}_{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we express the $b$'s in terms of $c$'s. Adding the equations, we get 

$$
{c}_{1}+{c}_{2}={b}_{1}\,⟹\,{b}_{1}={c}_{1}+{c}_{2}.
$$

Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
{c}_{1}=2({c}_{1}+{c}_{2})-{b}_{2}\,⟹\,{b}_{2}={c}_{1}+2{c}_{2}.
$$

Since $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2\end{aligned}]$, we can write the vector $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =4{b}_{1}-2{b}_{2} \\  & =4({c}_{1}+{c}_{2})-2({c}_{1}+2{c}_{2}) \\  & =4{c}_{1}+4{c}_{2}-2{c}_{1}-4{c}_{2} \\  & =2{c}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$
